text:
maria: quick update from today's token-budget sweep across A10/T4/L4/A100/H100 — ran focused experiments on max_batch_size vs max_tokens_per_batch. posting highlights + a short profiling snippet.

sam: nice, what was the main perf signal?

maria: two surprises: 1) small GPUs (A10/T4) hit better throughput when we limit max_batch and allow larger tokens-per-batch (amortizes kernel select overhead). 2) big GPUs (A100/H100) prefer letting max_batch grow — even with KV cache pressure — thanks to more efficient fused-gemm kernels past seq_len ~1024.

kevin: numbers?

maria: pasted the tight summary below (median throughput / p99 delta vs current defaults):

```
# per-GPU recommended sweep point (quick summary)
A10: max_batch=32, max_tokens_batch=512  -> +6% median, p99 -3%
T4:  max_batch=24, max_tokens_batch=448  -> +4% median, p99 +2% (kernel fallback case)
L4:  max_batch=48, max_tokens_batch=768  -> +8% median, p99 -5%
A100: max_batch=128, max_tokens_batch=1024 -> +12% median, p99 -7%
H100: max_batch=192, max_tokens_batch=1536 -> +15% median, p99 -10%
```

jen: that T4 p99 increase worries me — root cause?

maria: T4 hit a kernel-selection fallback at batch token sums near 400-480 where we switch from int8-optimized path to a safer fp16 GEMM due to alignment/tiling mismatch. That fallback increases tail latency.

lucas: any KV cache effects?

maria: yes — L4 showed increased page thrash when we allowed tokens_per_batch > 700. KV lookup cost grows non-linearly with total cached KV size + new token writes. Observed ~6% added latency for large batches on L4 unless we pin cache partitions.

kevin: could we change queue policy instead of per-gpu hard limits? e.g., token-budget-first queue that caps total tokens per formed batch, then respects a soft max_batch.

maria: that's exactly what I tried in the sweep. token-budget-first + prefer-low-latency route for small GPUs reduced median latency and avoided kernel fallback on T4 in most cases. Implementation: form batches by summing tokens and stop when tokens >= target_budget or count >= max_batch. target_budget tuned per-GPU.

sam: do you have the target_budget numbers?

maria: short list (these are conservative defaults we validated in 1h stress runs):

```
# token_budget targets (per GPU)
A10: 1024
T4:  896
L4:  1536
A100: 4096
H100: 6144
```

jen: how does kernel selection interact with those budgets? We need deterministic switching to avoid regressions.

maria: kernel selection is sequence-length and batch-dim dependent. For small GPUs the optimized int8 kernel is fastest up to seq_len ~512 and effective batch dims <48; for A100/H100 the fused kernels win for seq_len >=1024. So budgets should map to sequence length distributions: if an app commonly sends long sequences, prefer higher token budgets on big GPUs.

ci-bot: perf-regression-check: canary run with token-budget-first policy applied to eng-runtime/canary-2026-03-17 -> median improved 5.8%, p99 overall -4.1%. T4 p99 +1.9% (narrow cases).

lucas: thanks ci-bot. Action items:
- maria: open PR with per-GPU defaults + token-budget-first queue implementation (include an opt-in flag).
- kevin: run 24h KV stress on L4 with pinned partitioning to confirm no thrash.
- sam: update rollout playbook to include kernel-fallback telemetry and an automatic rollback threshold for T4 p99 regressions.

maria: yep, I'll draft the PR today. I'll include micro-profiles (nvprof traces) showing where the fallback happens and a small script to reproduce the T4 case.

jen: please add a note for ops: if KV cache writes exceed X GB/s on L4, force soft cap tokens_per_batch -> 700 and notify on-call.

maria: good call — will add alert + auto-cap.

sam: great. :thumbsup: keep the canary window open 48h and let's review on Monday.
